words.definition_en: a plan for how money will be spent
example_sentences: We need to stick to our budget this month.

words.definition_en: money received, especially from work
example_sentences: Her monthly income covers all her expenses.

words.definition_en: an amount of money spent on something
example_sentences: Housing is our biggest expense.

words.definition_en: money left after taxes and essential expenses
example_sentences: Rising prices have reduced people's disposable income.

words.definition_en: to have enough money to pay for something
example_sentences: We can't afford a new car right now.

words.definition_en: owing money
example_sentences: They got into debt after losing their jobs.

words.definition_en: phrasal verb: to finish paying a debt
example_sentences: It took five years to pay off the loan.

words.definition_en: an arrangement allowing you to withdraw more money than you have
example_sentences: He went into his overdraft at the end of the month.

words.definition_en: a bank account that earns interest on money kept in it
example_sentences: I put some money into my savings account every month.

words.definition_en: an automatic payment taken from a bank account regularly
example_sentences: My rent is paid by direct debit.

words.definition_en: a document requesting payment for goods or services
example_sentences: Please send the invoice by the end of the week.

words.definition_en: a document proving a payment was made
example_sentences: Keep the receipt in case you need to return it.

words.definition_en: able to be paid back
example_sentences: The deposit is fully refundable if you cancel in time.

words.definition_en: not able to be paid back
example_sentences: The ticket is non-refundable.

words.definition_en: the small, less obvious details of a contract, often important
example_sentences: Check the fine print before you agree to anything.

words.definition_en: a section of a legal document dealing with a particular point
example_sentences: There's a clause about early termination.

words.definition_en: having legal force and required to be followed
example_sentences: The agreement is legally binding once signed.

words.definition_en: failure to fulfil the terms of a contract
example_sentences: They sued the supplier for breach of contract.

words.definition_en: legally responsible for something
example_sentences: The company is liable for any damage caused.

words.definition_en: to take legal action against someone
example_sentences: She sued the company for unfair dismissal.

words.definition_en: to resolve a legal dispute without going to trial
example_sentences: The two companies settled out of court.

words.definition_en: to give evidence, especially in court
example_sentences: She was asked to testify in court.

words.definition_en: legal protections given to buyers of goods and services
example_sentences: Consumer rights protect you when a product is faulty.

words.definition_en: a written guarantee to repair or replace a faulty product
example_sentences: The laptop comes with a two-year warranty.

words.definition_en: having a fault; not working correctly
example_sentences: We returned the defective item for a refund.

words.definition_en: subject to tax
example_sentences: Only income above a certain amount is taxable.

words.definition_en: a document declaring income for tax purposes
example_sentences: He filed his tax return before the deadline.

words.definition_en: a way of avoiding a rule without breaking the law directly
example_sentences: The company exploited a tax loophole.

words.definition_en: something of value owned by a person or company
example_sentences: Property is one of their main assets.

words.definition_en: a debt or financial obligation
example_sentences: The company's liabilities exceeded its assets.

words.definition_en: units of ownership in a company
example_sentences: She bought shares in a technology company.

words.definition_en: a payment made by a company to its shareholders
example_sentences: The company pays an annual dividend.

words.definition_en: a general rise in prices over time
example_sentences: Inflation has made everyday goods more expensive.

words.definition_en: a period of economic decline
example_sentences: The country went into recession last year.

words.definition_en: the amount of money needed to cover basic expenses
example_sentences: The cost of living has risen sharply.

words.definition_en: idiom: to have just enough money to live on
example_sentences: They're struggling to make ends meet.

words.definition_en: to make neither a profit nor a loss
example_sentences: The business broke even after its second year.

words.definition_en: idiom: paying with your own money, often to be reimbursed later
example_sentences: I paid for the flights out of pocket.

words.definition_en: idiom: money saved for the future, especially retirement
example_sentences: They built a small nest egg over the years.

words.definition_en: idiom: to spend less money than before
example_sentences: We've had to tighten our belts since prices went up.

words.definition_en: to reduce spending
example_sentences: The company cut costs by reducing staff.
